analysis.evidence: מֵהָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ means “of the birds according to their kind.” The verse lists birds alongside livestock and ground creatures, with two of each to come. The singular עוֹף thus denotes birds as a class.
analysis.morphology: Partitive preposition מִן (מֵ־) + definite article הָ־ + masculine singular absolute collective noun.

analysis.evidence: In מֵהָעוֹף לְמִינֵהוּ, the masculine singular suffix refers to the collective הָעוֹף. The parallel הַבְּהֵמָה לְמִינָהּ uses a feminine singular suffix with its feminine antecedent. Both phrases classify the creatures by kind.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ plus masculine singular construct noun מִין with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־ֵהוּ.

draft.change: Add Gen.6.20 as evidence for the Hebrew partitive sense min-some-of in the existing min article.
draft.definition: Partitive מִן introduces a whole or group from which some members are taken or counted.
draft.evidence: In Gen.6.20, הַבְּהֵמָה names the group and שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל specifies two of each kind.

analysis.evidence: וּמִן הַבְּהֵמָה לְמִינָהּ means ‘and from among the livestock according to their kinds’. שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל, ‘two of each’, gives the number that will come from each kind.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + independent preposition מִן governing הַבְּהֵמָה ‘the livestock’. No suffix.
analysis.sense: Partitive. Introduces the group from which members are selected.

analysis.evidence: The verse lists birds, הַבְּהֵמָה, and creatures that creep on the ground. The following לְמִינָהּ, “according to its kind,” refers back to the feminine singular noun and presents it as a class of animals from which pairs will come to Noah.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with the definite article הַ־, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular suffix refers to הַבְּהֵמָה. The parallel phrases for birds and creeping things use לְמִינֵהוּ, showing that each group is classified by kind.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person feminine singular possessive suffix ־ָהּ.

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל רֶמֶשׂ הָאֲדָמָה, כֹּל qualifies רֶמֶשׂ “creeping thing.” The following לְמִינֵהוּ “according to its kind” makes the distribution clear. Two come from each kind.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with prefixed מִן “from.” The נ assimilates to the following כ, marked by dagesh.

analysis.evidence: In רֶמֶשׂ הָאֲדָמָה, “creeping creatures of the ground,” הָאֲדָמָה completes the construct phrase. The following לְמִינֵהוּ, “according to its kind,” groups these creatures by kind alongside the birds and livestock.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In מִכֹּל רֶמֶשׂ הָאֲדָמָה, “from every creeping thing of the ground,” הָאֲדָמָה completes the construct phrase and names the surface on which the creatures move.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth

analysis.evidence: In רֶמֶשׂ הָאֲדָמָה לְמִינֵהוּ, the masculine singular suffix refers to רֶמֶשׂ, the collective noun for creatures that creep on the ground. The phrase groups them by kind, as the parallel phrases do for birds and livestock.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־ֵהוּ.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל means “two of each.” The numeral gives the number from each kind that will come to Noah.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, masculine dual absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The repeated phrases לְמִינֵהוּ and לְמִינָהּ group the animals by kind. In שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל, “two of each,” מִן is partitive and כֹּל distributes the count of two over those kinds.
analysis.morphology: Preposition מִן with its נ assimilated to כ, followed by a masculine singular noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל identifies the subject as two of each kind of animal. אֵלֶיךָ (‘to you’) gives the direction of their movement: they will come to Noah.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural

analysis.evidence: שְׁנַיִם מִכֹּל יָבֹאוּ אֵלֶיךָ says that two of each kind will come to Noah. לְהַחֲיוֹת gives the purpose of their coming. The animals are the implied object of the causative verb.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed לְ expressing purpose
